milestones.title: Switch on a light
milestones.goal: A glowing light that you place and colour yourself.

steps.instruction: Read the code in the editor. What do you think will appear on the stage? Pick your guess, then press **Run** to find out.
choices: A glowing yellow circle in the middle of the stage
A glowing yellow circle in the top-left corner
steps.explain: `stage.circle(320, 200, 40, "butter", glow=True)` draws a circle. **320** is how far across (x) and **200** is how far down (y). The stage is 640 wide and 400 tall, so (320, 200) is right in the middle.

check.description: Your program ran and lit up the stage.

hints: Look at the last line, the one that starts with `stage.circle`.
`stage.circle(x, y, radius, colour)` draws a circle. x is how far across, y is how far down.
`stage.circle(100, 100, 20, "mint")` would draw a small mint circle near the top-left.
The circle is at x = 320 and y = 200. The stage is 640 wide and 400 tall. So it's in the ______ of the stage.
It draws one butter-yellow glowing circle in the middle of the stage. Pick that answer and press Run.

steps.instruction: Move the light to the **left side** of the stage. Change the first number inside `stage.circle(...)` to something smaller, like `100`. Then press **Run**.

check.description: Your light moved to the left!

hints: Look at the line with `stage.circle`. The first number inside the brackets is x.
x means how far across the stage. Small x is on the left. Big x is on the right.
`stage.circle(500, 200, 40, "butter", glow=True)` would put the light on the right side.
`stage.circle(___, 200, 40, "butter", glow=True)`: fill the blank with a number smaller than 200.
`stage.circle(100, 200, 40, "butter", glow=True)`. Type it yourself, then try a different small number too.

steps.instruction: Pick your own colour! Change `"butter"` to `"mint"`, `"coral"`, `"blossom"`, `"sky"` or `"lilac"`. Keep the quotes.
hints: The colour is the word in quotes inside `stage.circle(...)`.
Colour names are text, so they need quotes around them, like `"mint"`.
`stage.circle(100, 200, 40, "sky", glow=True)` draws a sky-blue light.
`stage.circle(100, 200, 40, "______", glow=True)`: put a colour name in the quotes.
`stage.circle(100, 200, 40, "coral", glow=True)`. Type it yourself, or pick another colour you like more.

milestones.title: Your name in lights
milestones.goal: Your own name, glowing on the stage.

steps.instruction: New code! Look at `name = "AARAV"`, and how the last line uses `name`. What will the stage show?
choices: An error, because name has no quotes on the last line
steps.explain: `name` is a **variable**: a box with a label. `name = "AARAV"` puts the text AARAV in the box. When you write `name` without quotes, Python opens the box and uses what's inside.
hints: Look at line 3, `name = "AARAV"`, and then at the last line.
A variable is a labelled box. The `=` puts something into the box.
If you write `pet = "Bruno"` and then use `pet`, Python uses Bruno.
`name` holds "_____", so the stage shows _____.
It shows AARAV glowing, because `name` holds the text AARAV.

steps.instruction: Make it **your** name. Change `"AARAV"` to your own name (keep the quotes!) and press **Run**. Your name stays on this device.
hints: Look at line 3: `name = "AARAV"`.
Text in Python goes inside quotes. The quotes tell Python it's words, not code.
`name = "Kabir"` would put Kabir in the name box.
`name = "______"`: your name goes between the quotes.
`name = "Meera"`, but with your own name. Type it yourself.

milestones.title: A light for every letter
milestones.goal: Each letter of your name in its own glowing light.

steps.instruction: This code has a **for loop**. What do you think it will print in the Output box?
choices: Each letter of your name on its own line
The word letter, printed again and again
steps.explain: A `for` loop repeats the indented lines once for each letter. Each time round, `letter` holds the next letter of your name, so `print(letter)` prints one letter per line.
hints: Look at the line `for letter in name:` and the line under it.
A for loop repeats the indented lines, once for each item.
`for animal in ["cat", "dog"]:` with `print(animal)` inside prints cat, then dog.
Each time round, `letter` is one ______ of your name.
It prints each letter of your name on its own line.

steps.instruction: Press **Run** first. Every light is drawn in the same spot, all on top of each other! Add this line **inside the loop**, lined up under `stage.text`, so each light moves along: `x = x + 60`

check.description: Every letter has its own light!

hints: Look at the loop. What changes each time round? Right now nothing changes x, so every light lands in the same spot.
Lines inside a loop have 4 spaces in front. A new line with the same 4 spaces runs every time round.

This draws three stars in a row:
`for star in range(3):`
`    stage.circle(x, 100, 10, "sky")`
`    x = x + 50`
Add `x = x + __` as the last line inside the loop, with 4 spaces in front.
Add `    x = x + 60` under the `stage.text` line, lined up with it. Type it yourself.

milestones.title: Light show!
milestones.goal: Your name flashing in new colours, again and again.

steps.instruction: Time for the show! The big loop flashes your lights again and again, with new random colours each time. Replace `___` with how many flashes you want (try `8`) and press **Run**.
hints: Look at line 5: `for flash in range(___):`.
`range(5)` makes a loop go round 5 times.
`for jump in range(3):` repeats the indented lines 3 times.
`for flash in range(_):`: put a number of 3 or more in the brackets.
`for flash in range(8):`. Type it yourself.

steps.instruction: Make it yours! Change at least one thing: the speed (the number in `stage.wait`), the number of flashes, the size of the lights (`26`) or the background colour (`"night"`). Then press **Run**.

check.description: That's your very own light show!

hints: Look for the numbers and colour names. Each one changes something about the show.
`stage.wait(0.4)` waits 0.4 seconds between flashes. Smaller is faster.
`stage.wait(0.1)` makes a super-fast show. `stage.background("pine")` changes the background.
Try `stage.wait(___)` with a different number, like 0.2.
Change `stage.wait(0.4)` to `stage.wait(0.15)` for a fast show. Type it yourself.

steps.instruction: Quick question before you finish: what does a `for` loop do?
choices: It makes the program run faster
It repeats the indented lines, once for each item
It draws a circle on the stage
steps.explain: A `for` loop repeats the lines indented under it, once for each item: each letter in a name, or each number in `range(8)`. You used two loops in your light show!
hints: Think about what happened in your light show.
One loop gave each letter a light. Another loop flashed the lights again and again.
`for flash in range(8):` ran its lines 8 times.
A for loop ______ the indented lines.
It repeats the indented lines, once for each item.
